subject: Viewing Coverages Probabilities layers generated by Survey Design in a GIS

messages.author: 512996ea4ff0ea65
messages.subject: Viewing Coverages Probabilities layers generated by Survey Design in a GIS
parts:
Hi everybody


I wonder if anybody has a recipe to use the coverage probabilities generated by the Design Survey module in DISTANCE and display them in any GIS as a raster layer. I am aware that this is probably more a GIS question.

What I managed to do is
1. Use the Grid generated by DISTANCE as a point shapfile. Then create a raster from the point feature.

2. Copy the data from Distance in the DATA Tab (Menu Data -> Copy data to clipboard), paste in Excel, save as txt file, load the table in ArcGis, and perform a Union with the created raster (take care of how to link vakues). 
However, for a strange reason one of the columns reads as character column (and morevoer, following Murphy´s law, the one I wanted most!!).

I tried to connect the database using the Arcgis protocolos, but I get values as if they were only integer (shoing all zeros).

Any advice welcome

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: Viewing Coverages Probabilities layers generated by Survey Design in a GIS
parts:
Hi Adrian,

I'm afraid I don't have a recipe to use the coverage as a raster layer, but I do have a small piece of advice that might help a bit.  The coverage probabilities are stored in the Distance project's Data File, which is always called DistData.mdb and lives in the Data Folder of the project (same place as the shapefiles).  If you open that file in Microsoft Access (don't upgrade the format, by the way), you'll see a table for each Data Layer in the project; if you look in the table associated with the coverage grid, you'll find a field that corresponds with each field for which a coverage has been generated.  There is also an ID field, which allows you to link the records to those in the shapefile (which has a LinkID field).  You can find out more about the format of the Data File in the help file "Appendix - Inside Distance", "Data File Reference".  Hope this helps,

 - Len

messages.subject: Fw: [distance-sampling] Viewing Coverages Probabilities layers generated by Survey Design in a GIS
parts:
Turns out the solution was as follows: Copy the data to an Excel file and edit the heads to leave only the field names before saving it to an Excel file. ArcGis 10.2. can read the Excel files as tables and then you can use Join.

For those who want to know about shapefiles in R including how you can add the LinkID required by Distance if you don't have GIS software read on...





Hi Adrian,

Not sure if I can help, I'm not familiar with working with rasters layers in GIS but if I wanted to associate the probabilities with the points in the grid shapefile I would try using R.

I would load the shapefile and the data into R and modify the attributes table there. Then you could enforce the values to be numeric.

Are you familiar with R? Here is some code you will need the shapefiles library too.

library(shapefiles)

#set your working directory to be the one with the shapefile - I take it you know you
#can find these in the .dat folder of the project? 

grid <- read.shapefile("Grid")              #miss out the extension and it will load it all
data <- read.csv("path/filename.csv") #or read.table, some way to get the data into R

#grid$dbf$dbf is the attrubute table
#so to add another column
test$dbf$dbf$new_column <- as.numeric(data$column)

#then you can view first 10 rows using
grid$dbf$dbf[1:10,]

write.shapefile(grid, "Grid_modified", arcgis=TRUE)

I am afraid I don't have access to GIS software right now to test this but that is how I add the LinkID column to the attribute table that Distance needs.

Let me know if this helps,

Laura
